messages:
Ryan (customer): Hey, ran into a spike of 5xxs from the hosted API since ~09:10 UTC, customers seeing timeouts and connection resets. curl shows TLS handshake timeout intermittently.
Maya (support): Sorry about that — can you paste the curl output and the request id you saw?
Ryan (customer): request-id=req_92a3, here's the curl: 
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxx'  
* Connected to api.redwood.example (13.45.23.11) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLS handshake timeout
* Failed to connect to api.redwood.example port 443: Operation timed out
```
Maya (support): Thanks. Seeing similar alert in our incident feed, escalated to SRE. tagging @Elena. Can you confirm if the client is behind a NAT/proxy?
Ryan (customer): Yes, this is an egress NAT in Azure. Only some customers affected — others fine.
Elena (sre): Looking at edge logs: multiple L4 connections established then TLS timeout at 1s. Early TLS alerts from edge-us-west/pool-7. Also seeing resolver errors from our edge to upstream resolvers: intermittent SERVFAIL and short timeouts.
Elena (sre): paste dig and tcpdump sample to thread:
```
; dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.example A 
13.45.23.11 13.45.23.12
; tcpdump on edge shows repeated retransmits to resolver 10.20.30.2 and RST from nat gateway
```
Maya (support): @Ryan can you run a quick dig from your NATed host? maybe EDNS0 truncation or MTU causing fallback to TCP which your gateway drops.
Ryan (customer): Ran dig +tcp: 
```
; dig +tcp api.redwood.example @10.20.30.2 A
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```
Maya (support): Oof. That aligns. @Jon can you check if our resolver handoff change earlier today could have introduced large UDP responses for records?
Jon (eng): We rolled a resolver handoff change around 08:55 that changes EDNS buffer size probing to prefer 1232. We didn't expect TCP fallback to be blocked. I'll check the rollout and the resolver health metrics.
deploy-bot: rollback candidate created for rollout 2026-03-17-resolver-handoff v2 -> paused
Elena (sre): In the meantime, workaround: add a short client-side retry with exponential backoff and fall back to another resolver or 1.1.1.1 via TCP allowed path. Also increasing TLS handshake timeout on our frontends from 1s to 3s reduces observed 502 rate by ~60% in canary.
Maya (support): Sharing repro steps for other customers: 1) curl with --resolve to force IP then reproduce handshake timeout 2) run dig +tcp against customer's resolver to confirm TCP blocked 3) capture pcap of NAT egress.
Ryan (customer): Confirmed; adding alternate resolvers dropped 5xxs. Can you notify when rollback complete?
Jon (eng): Rolling back resolver handoff now, will post when done.
infra-monitor: Metric spike: resolver.servfail.rate edge-us-west 3m avg -> 12% at 09:12 UTC :warning:
Jon (eng): Rollback completed at 09:28 UTC. Observability: resolver.servfail.rate back to baseline, TLS handshake timeouts dropped.
Maya (support): Great — @Ryan can you validate on your side and close if good?
Ryan (customer): Verified — error rate back to normal and no more handshake timeouts. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
Maya (support): I'll follow up with a post-incident note and suggested docs for customers behind restrictive NATs/proxies. :memo:
